on_match_fail_variant.when: a secret/PII pattern matches but replacement leaves residue (overlapping match, multi-line token, malformed replacement), OR the high-entropy fallback fires below
on_match_fail_variant.action: fail_on_unredactable:true raises and the runner emits NO redacted output for that artifact; it must not pass through the unmatched value
on_match_fail_variant.note: Top-level on_match stays 'replace' for named patterns. This variant is the explicit escape hatch that lets fail_on_unredactable fire (Phase 3 decision 4). Runner patch required - see high_entropy_fallback.note.

high_entropy_fallback.action: any probe run that (a) matches no named secret/PII pattern above yet (b) has Shannon entropy >= threshold and (c) is not in the runner allowlist (UUIDs, commit SHAs, base64 of known non-secrets) is treated as an unredactable secret: honor fail_on_unredactable (fail, do not emit).
high_entropy_fallback.note: RUNNER PATCH (follow-up, not in this policy-only change): (1) compile secret_patterns then pii_patterns with flags; (2) replace matches; (3) scan residue with regex_probe + entropy>=4.5, excluding allowlisted UUID/SHA shapes; (4) if any residue hit and fail_on_unredactable==true, throw UnredactableSecret and suppress artifact output; (5) also throw if on_match_fail_variant.when fires. Current runner only does step 1-2, so fail_on_unredactable can never fire today.

pii_patterns.name: phone_nanp
pii_patterns.note: 6A-4 (F-75): requires a parenthesised or separated area code and NANP-valid area/exchange leading digits; bare 10-digit runs (order ids, metrics) no longer match.

pii_patterns.name: ipv4_address
pii_patterns.note: 6A-4 (F-75): each octet is validated 0-255, so 999.999.999.999 and other non-address dotted runs no longer match; K1 fixture loopback endpoints are preserved via fixture_allowlist.

fixture_allowlist.description: 6A-4 (F-75): deterministic K1 fixture constants are non-secret; the redaction replacement steps (and the high-entropy fallback) skip these exact strings and anchored token patterns so K1 evidence stays legible. Session and CSRF tokens are NOT in this list: they must still be redacted.
fixture_allowlist.runner_contract: Replacement steps must consult this allowlist before the high-entropy fallback (so session and CSRF tokens still fail closed while K1 fixture constants pass). Runner implementation is 6B-0 server code (files/tools/redaction_runner.py); this change is policy-only.
